'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[2020–2021 Indian farmers' protest]]
**[[Agriculture in India|Farmer]]s vow to intensify their protest against laws aimed at liberalising [[agriculture]], after four farmers were rammed and killed yesterday in [[Uttar Pradesh]] by a vehicle owned by [[Minister of Home Affairs (India)|Minister of State for Home Affairs]] [[Ajay Kumar Mishra]]. Three members of the party and the driver of the vehicle were then killed by protesters. A journalist was also found dead today near the scene of the violence. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/10/4/india-lakhimpur-kheri-town-deaths-farmers-protest (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Islamic State–Taliban conflict]]
**The [[Taliban]] says it has "destroyed an [[Islamic State – Khorasan Province|IS–K]] cell" in [[Kabul]] following yesterday's bombing at a mosque during the memorial for the mother of Taliban spokesman [[Zabihullah Mujahid]]. Mujahid says that a special Taliban unit carried out the operation and that the base was destroyed and everyone inside was killed. [https://www.dw.com/en/taliban-destroy-is-k-cell-after-kabul-mosque-bombing/a-59396833 (Deutsche Welle)]
*[[Insurgency in the Maghreb]]
**Twelve [[Burkina Faso Armed Forces|Burkinabé troops]] are killed and five others are wounded in an attack in the northern [[Sanmatenga Province]]. No group has claimed responsibility for the [[ambush]] assault. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/militants-kill-eight-soldiers-injure-five-burkina-faso-attack-2021-10-04/ (Reuters)]
*Aftermath of the [[Second Libyan Civil War]]
**A [[United Nations]] report blames all warring sides in [[Libya]] of committing [[war crime]]s and [[crimes against humanity]], particularly against detainees, migrants and prominent women. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/10/4/libyas-warring-sides-may-be-guilty-of-war-crimes-un-probe (Al Jazeera)]
*Police in [[Cyprus]] arrest a man suspected of "planning attacks against [[Israel]]i people". Israel has accused [[Iran]] of orchestrating the plot, although Iran has denied the allegations. Other reports suggest that the target of the plot was businessman [[Teddy Sagi]] and could be linked to business disputes involving Sagi. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-middle-east-58714131 (BBC News)]
*Four [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|ISIL]] terrorists and one security forces member are killed during clashes in southern [[Khartoum]], [[Sudan]]. Four other suspected militants are arrested during the raid, while three more soldiers are wounded. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/sudanese-security-forces-clash-with-terrorist-cell-khartoum-state-tv-2021-10-04/ (Reuters)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Evergrande liquidity crisis]]
**Chinese state-run [[Chinese tabloid|tabloid]] ''[[Global Times]]'' reports that Chinese property developer [[Evergrande Group]] will sell 51% of its property service arm to rival company [[Hopson Development]] for [[United States dollar|US$]]5 billion. The report comes as both Hopson and Evergrande suspended [[Stock trader|trading in their shares]] on the [[Hong Kong Stock Exchange]] in the morning, pending an announcement about a "major transaction". [https://www.cnbc.com/2021/10/04/evergrande-set-to-sell-part-of-stake-in-property-services-unit.html (CNBC)] [https://www.thejakartapost.com/news/2021/10/04/property-giant-china-evergrande-suspends-hong-kong-market-trading.html (AFP via ''The Jakarta Post'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2021 North Indian Ocean cyclone season]]
**The death toll from the floods in [[Muscat]], [[Oman]], caused by [[Cyclones Gulab and Shaheen|Cyclone Shaheen]], increases to 12 as nine more people are found dead. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/10/4/uae-saudi-arabia-brace-for-cyclone-shaheen-after-oman-landfall (Al Jazeera)]
*[[2021 Cumbre Vieja volcanic eruption]]
**The main cone of the [[Cumbre Vieja]] [[volcano]] on the [[Canary Islands|island]] of [[La Palma]] collapses, increasing the lava flow into the [[Atlantic Ocean]]. The main lava flow is now 1.2 km across at its widest point. [https://english.elpais.com/society/2021-10-04/volcanic-eruption-in-la-palma-part-of-cone-collapses-increasing-lava-flow.html (''El Pais'')]
*[[2021 Orange County oil spill]]
**Authorities in [[Orange County, California]], United States, blame a 41-year-old oil pipeline for yesterday's spill, so far releasing 3,000 barrels of oil into the Pacific Ocean and severely damaging the coast of [[Southern California]]. [https://www.reuters.com/business/environment/investigators-probing-cause-major-california-offshore-oil-spill-2021-10-04/ (Reuters)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]], [[COVID-19 drug development]]
****The [[Australia]]n [[Australian Government|government]] signs an agreement with [[Merck Sharp & Dohme]] to buy 300,000 courses of the antiviral drug [[molnupiravir]], pending regulator clearance, which would be the first pill to treat COVID-19 patients. [https://www.9news.com.au/national/coronavirus-australia-treatment-covid-pill-molnupiravir-may-be-ready-for-use-in-australia-by-2020-after-deal-made-with-merck-sharp--dohme/0f04b8fb-2d9d-443d-beb9-ce2a1a48abd3 (9 News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Fiji]]
****[[Fiji]] reopens businesses, [[Place of worship|places of worship]] and educational institutions at 70% capacity to those who have been [[COVID-19 vaccination in Fiji|fully vaccinated]] amid a decrease in the number of new cases and an increase in the vaccination rate. [https://matangitonga.to/2021/10/04/fiji-businesses-re-open-after-months-lockdown (''Matangi Tonga'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand]]
****[[New Zealand]] drops the elimination strategy to combat [[COVID-19]] in favour of a new model that contains [[COVID-19 vaccination in New Zealand|vaccination rates]] amid the continued outbreak of the [[SARS-CoV-2 Delta variant]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/oct/04/new-zealand-covid-strategy-in-transition-ardern-says-as-auckland-awaits-lockdown-decision (''The Guardian'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Isle of Man]]
****The [[Isle of Man]] begins administering booster shots of the [[COVID-19 vaccine]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-isle-of-man-58768063 (BBC News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Sweden]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Sweden]]
****The [[Public Health Agency of Sweden]] recommends that children between the ages of 12 and 15 be vaccinated against COVID-19 using the [[Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine]]. [https://www.straitstimes.com/world/europe/sweden-recommends-pfizer-covid-19-vaccine-for-children-aged-12-to-15-rejects-moderna (''The Straits Times'')]
***[[European Union response to the COVID-19 pandemic]], COVID-19 vaccine
****The [[European Medicines Agency]] approves a third dose of the [[Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine]] for people aged over 18-years-old. However, it was up to member states to decide whether to use them. [https://www.dw.com/en/covid-eu-regulator-backs-biontech-pfizer-vaccine-booster-for-18-and-over/a-59404536 (Deutsche Welle)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Thailand]]
***[[Thailand]] begins a vaccination programme for children between the ages of 12 and 17 years old using the Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine as the [[Government of Thailand|government]] plans to resume face-to-face learning. [https://www3.nhk.or.jp/nhkworld/en/news/20211004_24/ (NHK World-Japan)]
*[[Insulate Britain protests]]
**Insulate Britain holds a [[sit-in]] protest in three major routes into [[London]], including the [[Blackwall Tunnel]]. The group have stated that they will continue protesting until [[Government of the United Kingdom|the government]] has concrete plans to [[Retrofitting|retrofit]] around 29 million buildings which the group claims have insufficient [[Building insulation|insulation]]. [https://www.itv.com/news/2021-10-04/insulate-britain-block-major-london-routes-including-blackwall-tunnel (ITV News)]

'''International relations'''
*[[2021 North Kosovo protests]]
**[[Kosovo]] and [[Serbia]] begin implementing stickers to cover national symbols and country abbreviations on their respective [[Vehicle registration plate|vehicle license plates]] when they are in the other country, with normal traffic on the border fully resuming. [https://exit.al/en/2021/10/04/kosovo-implements-brussels-agreement-with-serbia-over-license-plates/ (Exit News)]
*[[North Korea–South Korea relations]]
**The [[Government of North Korea|North]] and [[Government of South Korea|South Korean governments]] reinstate the [[Seoul–Pyongyang hotline]] after North Korea suspended the connection in early August, in protest against [[Republic of Korea Armed Forces|South Korea's]] [[military exercise]]s with the [[United States Armed Forces|United States]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20211004-north-and-south-korea-restore-cross-border-hotline (AFP via France 24)]
*[[Cross-Strait relations]] 
**A total of 52 [[People's Liberation Army Air Force]] aircraft fly into Taiwan's southwestern air defense identification zone, the Ministry of National Defense says on Twitter. This amounts to 145 Chinese aircraft which have flown into Taiwan's air defense area this month [https://www.nbcnews.com/think/opinion/chinese-warplanes-fly-toward-taiwan-alarm-u-s-display-only-ncna1280856 (NBC News)]

'''Law and crime'''
*Aftermath of the [[2021 Myanmar coup d'état]]
**Deposed leader [[Aung San Suu Kyi]] asks to reduce her time in court appearances, stating that her health has deteriorated. The judge will make a decision on the request next week. Suu Kyi currently faces multiple charges ranging from corruption to money laundering. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/oct/04/aung-san-suu-kyi-asks-to-reduce-court-time-due-to-strained-health (''The Guardian'')]
*A U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) special agent is killed and another is critically wounded, and a [[Tucson Police Department]] officer is wounded at a shooting involving two suspects, one of whom was a gunman who is believed to have killed himself, at the [[Tucson, Arizona]] [[Amtrak]] train station; the officers had boarded the just-disembarked [[Sunset Limited]] to do a drug check. [https://www.msn.com/en-us/news/us/dea-agent-killed-in-arizona-amtrak-shooting-was-noted-leader/ar-AAPaMFz?ocid=msedgdhp&pc=W000 (MSN/AP)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*The [[parliament of Singapore]] passes a law aimed to outlaw [[Interventionism (politics)|foreign interference in domestic affairs]]. Opponents of the measure have expressed concerns regarding the broadness of certain provisions that may potentially hinder some [[civil liberties]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/oct/05/singapore-passes-foreign-interference-law-allowing-authorities-to-block-internet-content (AFP via ''The Guardian'')]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[2021 Facebook outage]]
**[[Facebook]], [[Instagram]], [[WhatsApp]], and [[Oculus (brand)|Oculus]] experience an extended global outage that began at 15:39 [[Coordinated Universal Time|UTC]]. Some experts believe that the outage was caused by a [[Border Gateway Protocol|BGP]] update from Facebook. [https://www.cnn.com/2021/10/04/tech/facebook-instagram-whatsapp-outage/index.html (CNN)] [https://cfl.re/3l7WBQs (Cloudflare)]
*Scientists [[David Julius]] and [[Ardem Patapoutian]] are awarded the 2021 [[Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine]] "for their discoveries of receptors for temperature and touch". [https://www.reuters.com/business/healthcare-pharmaceuticals/julius-patapoutian-win-2021-nobel-prize-medicine-2021-10-04/ (Reuters)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2021 NASCAR Cup Series]]
**[[Bubba Wallace|Darrell "Bubba" Wallace Jr.]] wins the rain-shortened [[YellaWood 500]] at [[Talladega Superspeedway]], becoming the first African-American to win a NASCAR Cup race since 1963. [https://www.nytimes.com/2021/10/04/sports/autoracing/nascar-bubba-wallace-talladega.html (''The New York Times'')]
